about.title: Rohnert Park Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Falls happen fast, but the aftermath can drag on for months. Whether it happened on a wet floor near Rohnert Park Expressway, a cracked walkway off Redwood Drive, or a poorly lit stairwell near Golf Course Drive, the moments after a fall matter. California law asks whether the property owner knew, or should have known, about the hazard and failed to address it. That's why photos of the scene, witness names, and any surveillance footage can shape the outcome of a claim. Rohnert Park's mix of retail centers, apartment communities, and public spaces means falls can happen almost anywhere property isn't kept up. LawProactive doesn't practice law or represent you directly. Instead, we connect you at no cost with an independent attorney in our network who can review what happened, explain your options under California's premises liability rules, and help you understand your next steps without any pressure.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney About a Rohnert Park Fall

items.title: Notice Has to Be Shown
items.desc: California law requires proving the property owner knew or reasonably should have known about the hazard. An attorney can help gather the evidence needed to establish that notice existed.

items.title: Surveillance Footage Disappears Fast
items.desc: Many businesses overwrite security video within days or weeks. Acting quickly to request preservation of footage can make a meaningful difference in a claim.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce, Not Eliminate, Recovery
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, so even if you're found partly responsible for the fall, you may still be entitled to pursue compensation for the remaining share.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Rohnert Park?
items.answer: In California, you generally have two years from the date of the fall to file a claim against a private property owner. If a government-owned property, like a public sidewalk or building, is involved, the deadline is much shorter and requires a separate claims process. It's best to talk with an attorney as soon as possible to avoid missing a critical deadline.

items.question: What if the store or landlord says I was careless?
items.answer: Property owners and their insurers often argue the injured person wasn't paying attention. Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still recover compensation even if you share some responsibility, though the amount may be adjusted accordingly. An attorney can help push back against unfair blame.

items.question: Does it matter where in Rohnert Park the fall happened?
items.answer: Yes, the type of property and its condition matter more than the exact address. Falls near busy retail and commercial areas along corridors like Redwood Drive or Rohnert Park Expressway often involve high foot traffic, which can affect how quickly hazards should have been noticed and fixed. An attorney can look at the specific circumstances of your fall to assess the claim.
